newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-AGF looks for strong full year.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-AGF looks for strong full year.

text.p: The head of Assurances Generales de France said on Friday the insurer hoped to double first-half profit in the full year but would need a little luck to do it.

"Our objective is to double what we did in the first half," AGF Chairman Antoine Jeancourt Galignani told Reuters Financial Television in an interview. "We will need a lot of energy which I'm sure we have but also some luck."
"In our business, if you have some natural catastrophes, if you have a hurricane, a typhoon...an unforecast downward development of the financial market, that can have some impact."
France's second-largest insurer, privatised last May, said Thursday consolidated net profit rose to 723 million francs from 487 million on premium income which rose 5.4 percent to 33.8 billion.
Galignani rejected suggestions made by some analysts that AGF had relied overly on capital gains to produce the profit increase.
"The capital gains we made are about half of what we made last year...we have been improving very much our technical profit and our underwriting profit," he said in the interview.
At the same time, he said it was natural, given its large equity stakes AGF should realise some capital gains.
He said the non-life sector was still improving in France. "We think there's still some good news to come," he said. AGF posted a 12 percent rise in non-life insurance profits.
He was also upbeat on the company's overseas activities.
"We're now very profitable in Spain, we've strong growth in Brazil, southeast Asia. We've also very respectable growth with our German associate," he said.

As far as further expansion, "the name of the game is to strengthen ourselves in sectors or companies where we can get a strong contribution to our profits." He cited transport and credit insurance, areas in which AGF was already strong, as potential areas for growth.
He said AGF was particularly interested in investing in emerging countries where goodwill costs were low. "We don't want to pay goodwill."
He added he believed a turnaround was near for its banking and financial operations. "We are quite confident."
He praised the performance of its real estate lending arm Comptoir des Entrepreneurs which more than halved its losses.
"The new management has said ...it wants to be in the black next year and quite frankly they're on track," he said.
He added AGF and Comptoir were developing more synergies. "Our networks are selling mortgage products. We're thinking of products that couple mortgage products and life products."
He said, however, AGF wanted to dispose of Banque du Phenix, whose loss rose to 51 million from a loss of 36 million, as soon as possible.
"We're having discussions with a number of interested parties but it is too early to say when we are going to achieve a sale."
The loss from banking activities grew to 346 million from a loss of 203 million but that reflected a 245 million franc addition to reserves to cover anticipated costs from the sale of Phenix.
He said he was disappointed at the lacklustre performance of AGF's share price since privatisation.

"It hasn't been going up as much as we hoped. The only thing we can do is work hard and show shareholders and investors we're really determined to do what we said wed would do -- to get the earning per share where we wanted in 1997 at twice the low point of 1994," he said.
AGF shares closed up 1.5 francs at 140. It was sold to institutions at 136 francs per share and small shareholders at 128 francs.
